title: Your first number
idea: Figure, year, producer: a sentence you can defend.
summary: Anyone can find a number on data.un.org. Making it hold up in a report takes three more seconds: the unit, the year, and the agency that measured it.

transcript.text: You have been asked for a figure, and it has to hold up.
Everything starts at one address: data dot U N dot org. One search box over eighty-five thousand official statistics.
Type it the way you would say it out loud. Name the measure, and name the country.
A couple of seconds later, you have an answer.
First, check this chip. It is the place the platform decided you meant. Leave the country out of your question, and it still picks one.
Now the number. One hundred and fifteen. On its own, that is not evidence. It is just a number on a screen.
So read the two lines underneath it. The unit: count per one hundred thousand live births. And the year: twenty twenty-three.
Then the part most people miss: the source. The Global S D G Database measured this. Data dot U N dot org is only how you found it.
And the chart on the left gives you the trend behind that single figure.
The figure, the year, the producer. Three things, every time, and you have a sentence you can defend.
